Tara — thanks for the clear list. High level: we support region-pinning for Hosted (US, EU) and full control in Dedicated/Private. Retention windows can be configured at contract time; common options are 30/90/365 days — Enterprise contracts can extend to 180 days or custom windows with a small fee (and a documented data handling plan). Deletion is implemented as follows in hosted:

- At the end of the retention window we trigger a coordinated delete job that removes user payloads and generated outputs from live stores and KV caches.
- Indexes and logs are soft-deleted immediately and permanently purged from primary storage within 48–72 hours.
- Backups are rotated; any snapshot older than the retention window is scheduled for secure wipe and overwriting; final purge usually within 7 days of snapshot expiry.

I'll let Mina and Vivek add the technical/attestation details and attach the policy doc and a draft SLA amendment. For procurement, I can prepare an order-form clause that enumerates the chosen retention windows and a simple deletion attestation process (PDF delivered within 5 business days of customer request).

Hi Tara — following up with a concise, actionable draft that you can drop into an order form or SOW. This note covers Hosted behavior; Dedicated/Private customers get the same deletion semantics but with customer-managed backups and the option to perform onsite deletion verifications.

Draft order-form language (suggested):

1) Data residency: Customer data shall be stored and processed in the region(s) selected at contract signing (US: us-west-1; EU: eu-central-1). Redwood shall not transfer Customer Data outside the selected region(s) except as required to comply with law, to provide redundancy in the same geopolitical region, or with Customer's prior written consent.

2) Retention windows (select one or specify custom): 30 days | 90 days (default) | 180 days (Enterprise) | 365 days | Custom (negotiated). Retention begins at the time of data ingestion.

3) Deletion semantics:
- Active data (conversation text, model prompts, generated outputs, KV cache entries) shall be removed from primary serving stores at the expiration of the applicable retention window.
- Soft-delete markers are applied immediately; subsequent permanent purges occur within 48–72 hours for primary stores.
- Audit logs that reference deletion events are retained for 365 days unless otherwise specified.
- Backups/snapshots: Snapshots older than the retention window will be scheduled for secure overwrite; final destruction is targeted within 7 calendar days of snapshot expiry.

4) Evidence and attestation: Upon Customer request Redwood will provide:
- A deletion report summarizing the deletion job (objects targeted, timestamps) within five (5) business days.
- Exportable audit logs for the deletion event (in machine-readable JSON or CSV).
- Optionally, a signed deletion certificate for an additional fee.

5) Exceptions: Certain ephemeral telemetry used for platform health and billing (aggregated and pseudonymized) may be retained beyond the selected window for up to 180 days; individual-level telemetry is treated as Customer Data and follows the retention window.

Operational notes: if MedTechCo requires a 180-day window we will convert the account to Enterprise plan with a short amendment. Deletion jobs are asynchronous — typical time-to-permanent-purge is 48–72 hours after the retention boundary. In the unlikely event a restoration is needed (restore window), that must be initiated within 7 days of deletion via support escalation; otherwise deletion is irreversible.

Attached: sla-amendment-template.docx (word template for clause insertion)

Let me know if you need a tighter purge SLA (we can discuss a 24–48 hour hard SLA for Dedicated customers with additional operational controls).

— Mina Haddad
Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
